reply_text:
I'll check the Zai window, read the paper abstract, and look at what "futon-related scopes" mining would mean in the mission before proposing packets.Pool is sized (208 futon-mission records). I'm now wiring two small additions, open ports as cross-session answer targets in the inputs and the validator, before dispatching.Fixing a test fixture (the sidecar act is missing a required key), and writing the batch-3 packet in parallel.Both packets are committed; dispatching them now to two idle Codex seats with parks.㊥ (gist) Batch 3 of the Zai mining is running on three seats against the fresh five-hour window, and two front-end packets are out: a KnowTeX-style dependency graph of a mission's acts for 象, and a read-only comparison of KnowTeX's rules against futon6's paper hypergraph. Five jobs are parked; nothing needs you now.

㊟ ("zai mining of Futon related scopes") I read this as the scope relation across turns, labelled over the futon missions. The pool is every unlabelled eligible operator turn stamped with a futon mission (not M-diagramprover): 208 records in five missions. Only 24 of them carry marked reply paragraphs, so this batch is mostly your own fragments (503) and their scopes. If you meant something else by scopes, say so and I'll redirect the second wave.

㊢ (batch 3) Each input now carries `mission_id` and the kernel's still-open ports at that record, so a labeller can say that a fragment sits within, or a paragraph answers, something opened in an earlier turn. The validator accepts those ids as targets. Packet, pool and harness changes are committed.

㊭ (second wave) The monthly meter was 73% used at 20:06Z and resets at 02:04Z, so what is unspent by then is lost. When these three return I'll read the window and, if it has room, send the M-diagramprover pool (114 records, the richest in reply acts) to zai-4 and zai-5, which claude-15 has finished with.

🈖 ("inspired by this paper") [KnowTeX](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15294) draws theorems and proofs as a dependency graph from LaTeX with two edge sources, manual `\uses{}` and inferred rules, three edge styles, red cycles, and an edge review table where the author deletes or adds edges and exports the corrections. 象 has the same two sources over acts: the Zai-labelled incidences and the kernel's port closes. The review table is the piece we lacked: your verdicts on edges are a measurement that does not reward closing ports.

㊢ (front-end packets) codex-57 builds `graph/build_mission_graph.py`: one column per session, labelled edges beside kernel closes, agreed edges marked, Tarjan cycles red, an export of your verdicts as a JSON file whose format a later scorer reads. No graphviz on this host, so the layout is a time-layered SVG. codex-47 writes a futon6 note only: which of KnowTeX's eight rules the classical arm of `paper_hypergraph.py` already has (the default proof association and ref-in-proof visibly), measured on three golden papers, and the smallest viewer change. Jobs `invoke-1791835856732-7830-135d2c43` and `invoke-1791835860976-7831-1e38cf16`, both running.

㊩ (one slip, fixed) My first batch-3 commit went in with a failing test because the chain checked the wrong exit code. The failure was in the fixture, not the behaviour; the follow-up commit fixes it and the ten harness tests pass.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("I haven't pressed enter") The half you have seen is the reading; the half not yet seen is whether an agent given that text behaves as if it had been in the conversation. When you do press enter, ask claude-19 something a previous seat already settled, say which of the two clock sources holds a seat's mission, or what was decided about session end. Its answer, right or wrong, is the first real data point, and the brief it saw is recorded under its timestamp so the two can be compared later.
